articles.author: Jaideep Parashar
articles.description:
You don’t need to be a full-time writer to publish a book anymore.
If you have expertise in any field, you can turn it into a book using AI tools — without losing your unique voice.
I’ve done this 40+ times, writing bestselling books on AI, productivity, and business, and today I’m sharing the exact process.

🧠 Why Write a Book in the AI Era?
Builds authority instantly
Opens doors to speaking, consulting, and partnerships
Creates passive income streams
Becomes a 24/7 credibility asset for your brand
And now, with AI, the process is faster, less overwhelming, and more structured.
🔄 My 6-Step AI-Powered Book Creation Process
Who do I want to help?
What’s the problem I can solve for them?
Why am I the right person to write this?
💡 AI Prompt:
“You are my book coach. Ask me 5 questions to clarify my book’s topic, audience, and main promise.”
2️⃣ Create a Table of Contents with AI
💡 AI Prompt:
“Create a 12-chapter table of contents for a beginner-friendly book on [topic]. Include chapter titles and 2–3 bullet points for each.”
3️⃣ Use AI for Research & Drafting
Topic research
Idea exploration
Outlining sections
However, I never use AI to write the book — I add my voice and insights. 
4️⃣ Write in Batches
5️⃣ Edit Like a Human, Polish Like AI
💡 AI Prompt:
“Edit this chapter for clarity, flow, and engagement, while keeping my personal tone intact.”
6️⃣ Design, Format & Publish
Use Canva or Fiverr for covers
Format in Microsoft Word or Vellum
Publish on Amazon KDP for global reach
📘 Real Example: ChatGPT Prompts for Excel
Defined audience: professionals working with Excel daily
Used AI to brainstorm 500+ prompts
Added real business use cases
Result: Amazon bestseller with continuous global sales
🧠 Pro Tip
📌 Final Thought
📘 Want My Full Book Creation Prompt Library?
See All My Books on Amazon

articles.author: datnm555
articles.description:
Introduction to Multithreading


Multithreading represents a fundamental computational model that empowers a single program (process) to execute multiple tasks simultaneously. These concurrent execution units, known as threads, are lightweight components that share process resources including memory space and file handles.
While multithreading delivers significant performance improvements and creates more responsive applications, it introduces complex challenges around synchronization, inter-thread communication, and potential race conditions. Multithreading design patterns serve as proven, reusable solutions to these common concurrent programming challenges.
